items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: The band leader was an ex-Navy officer who played the violin... So I said, “What is this?”... So she said, “Let me hear you play the piano.”... So from the first day, yeah.

ctx.x: When was the first time that you might have had to deal with chord symbols, or just a lead sheet as opposed to a written score?

When I got the job. As I said the manager asked me, I saw this “pianist wanted.” So I go inside and the manager came out and he said, “Can you play piano?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Well come in at 7:00 tonight” — it could be 6:00, it was early. And so I go there and I see five people. The band leader was an ex-Navy officer who played the violin. And there was a great — violin and accordion and drums and a piano, and alto saxophone. No bass. And that’s the first time I saw a chord symbol. And I’d never seen them…
So then this person would show you what major seven meant and all those kinds of things.
